footnotes: Seipel 1999 gives inscription as follows: “CHRISTIAN KOFAHL: A: 1677”.

Laubhold 2000: 259 speculates that the two slide tubes were switched at some point in the instrument’s history, as it
is quite unusual for the ascending bore to be smaller than the descending bore.
dimensions: bo1 10.45, bo2 10.1,²  be 74.5, le 1320, thickness of metal ca. .5, slide sec. 778, bell sec. 542.
remarks: Tubular slide stays. Bumper guard on slide bow. One flat bell stay, richly engraved. Ring in bell bow. Toothed seam at inner edge of garland. Garland attached by bending the edge of the bell outward. This is the oldest known surviving soprano trombone.
